item.title: The contract
item.description:
The contract is two protobuf packages under proto/, ledger.v1 and wallet.v1, generated into ledgerpb and walletpb.

The ledger’s service

proto/ledger/v1/ledger.proto declares five methods:

service Ledger {
 rpc OpenAccount(OpenAccountRequest) returns (OpenAccountResponse);
 rpc GetAccount(GetAccountRequest) returns (GetAccountResponse);
 rpc Deposit(DepositRequest) returns (DepositResponse);
 rpc Transfer(TransferRequest) returns (TransferResponse);
 rpc WatchAccount(WatchAccountRequest) returns (stream WatchAccountResponse);
}

An account is its ID, its balance, and when the balance last changed. A transfer is its ID, the two accounts, the amount and when it was made. Amounts are whole cents, in one currency:

message Account {
 string id = 1;
 int64 balance_cents = 2;
 google.protobuf.Timestamp balance_change_time = 3;
}

message Transfer {
 string id = 1;
 string from_account_id = 2;
 string to_account_id = 3;
 int64 amount_cents = 4;
 google.protobuf.Timestamp create_time = 5;
}

A transfer’s request carries its ID, so a transfer sent twice is posted once:

item.title: The ledger's accounts
item.description:
The ledger keeps its accounts and its transfers in two PostgreSQL tables, and moves money between accounts in one transaction per transfer, so money is never made or lost.

schema.sql

ledger/store/schema.sql makes the accounts, and the ledger’s own external account, which deposits come from:

CREATE TABLE accounts (
 id text PRIMARY KEY,
 balance_cents bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
 balance_changed_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
 CHECK (id = 'external' OR balance_cents >= 0)
);

INSERT INTO accounts (id) VALUES ('external');

The CHECK refuses a balance below zero for every account but external. external’s balance is the negative of every deposit, so the balances always sum to zero.

item.title: Serving the ledger
item.description:
The ledger’s server package is ledger.v1.Ledger, on the Store.

The methods

Method Answers
OpenAccount the account, opened with a zero balance, or as it is if it was already open
GetAccount the account, or NotFound
Deposit the deposit, as a transfer from external. NotFound for no such account
Transfer the transfer. FailedPrecondition when the source’s balance is short, NotFound for either account, InvalidArgument for an amount that isn’t positive or an account sent to itself, and AlreadyExists for a transfer’s ID reused for another transfer
WatchAccount the account at once, then again each time its balance changes. NotFound for no such account

item.title: Calling the ledger
item.description:
The wallet has one grpcclient Client for the ledger. Every method and readiness go through it.

The client’s settings

The wallet’s readSettings starts from grpcclient.DefaultSettings(), and sets the ledger’s address, the CA it trusts the ledger through, and the client certificate it presents:

ledger := grpcclient.DefaultSettings()
ledger.Addr = r.Get(env("LEDGER_ADDR").Validate(grpcclient.CheckAddr))
ledger.TLS = &tls.Config{
	RootCAs: r.Get(file("LEDGER_CA_FILE").Parse(certPool)),
	GetClientCertificate: r.Get(pemFile("LEDGER_TLS_PEM_FILE").Map(func(c *tls.Config) clientCertificate {
		return c.GetClientCertificate
	})),
	MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12,
}
ledger.Timeout = r.Get(env("LEDGER_TIMEOUT").Parse(time.ParseDuration).Default(ledger.Timeout).Validate(grpcclient.CheckTimeout))
ledger.MaxAttempts = r.Get(env("LEDGER_MAX_ATTEMPTS").Parse(strconv.Atoi).Default(ledger.MaxAttempts).Validate(grpcclient.CheckMaxAttempts))
ledger.ForwardScenario = true

type (
	serverCertificate = func(*tls.ClientHelloInfo) (*tls.Certificate, error)
	clientCertificate = func(*tls.CertificateRequestInfo) (*tls.Certificate, error)
)

The client

item.title: Serving the wallet
item.description:
The wallet’s server package is wallet.v1.Wallet, on the ledger’s generated client.

The methods

Method Needs Answers
OpenAccount wallet:write the caller’s account, opened in the ledger
GetAccount wallet:read the caller’s account
Send wallet:write the transfer from the caller’s account, to the account it names
WatchAccount wallet:read the caller’s account, as the ledger’s watch sends it

The claims and the scopes

A token’s claims are its subject and its scopes:

const (
	ScopeRead = "wallet:read"
	ScopeWrite = "wallet:write"
)

type Claims struct {
	Subject string `json:"sub"`
	Scope string `json:"scope"`
}

func (c Claims) HasScope(scope string) bool {
	return slices.Contains(strings.Fields(c.Scope), scope)
}

The fetched key set

item.title: Init
item.description:
The wallet’s settings

Everything the wallet’s Init reads, in one struct:

type settings struct {
	GRPC grpcserver.Settings
	Probes grpchealth.Settings
	Ledger grpcclient.Settings
	KeySet keySetSettings
	JWT jwt.Settings
	FaultTrustScope string
}

type keySetSettings struct {
	URL *url.URL
	Client httpclient.Settings
}

config.Struct sources and checks each one. A bad one makes Init fail, and the wallet exits 78, naming its variable:

func readSettings(ctx context.Context, s *humus.Setup) (settings, error) {
	env := func(name string) config.Value[string] { return config.Env(s.Process.Environment, name) }
	file := func(name string) config.Value[[]byte] { return env(name).Parse(readFile(s.Host.FS)) }
	pemFile := func(name string) config.Value[*tls.Config] { return env(name).Parse(pemTLS(s.Host.FS)) }

item.title: Testing
item.description:
The ledger’s unit tests

The ledger’s server takes a Store, so its tests give it a fake one, in memory, that fails when the test says so:

func (f *fakeStore) Account(_ context.Context, id string) (store.Account, error) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	f.reads++
	if f.err != nil {
		return store.Account{}, fmt.Errorf("reading account %s: %w", id, f.err)
	}
	a, ok := f.accounts[id]
	if !ok {
		return store.Account{}, fmt.Errorf("reading account %s: %w", id, store.ErrNotFound)
	}
	return a, nil
}

Each test serves it on the humustest Host, over TLS, and calls it with the ledger’s generated client:

item.title: Deploying
item.description:
The image

One image holds the wallet and the ledger. A Go stage builds each of them static, and the image copies them to /wallet and /ledger on a distroless base, to run as the non-root user 65532. example/grpc/wallet/Dockerfile names the exact images and their versions.

Build it from the repository’s root, since the module replaces humus and humus/grpc with their directories:

docker build --file example/grpc/wallet/Dockerfile --tag wallet .

item.title: Observing
item.description:
Opening Grafana

up.sh generates Grafana’s admin password into the grafana-admin Secret. Read it, then forward Grafana’s port:

kubectl --context kind-kind --namespace wallet get secret grafana-admin \
 --output jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 --decode
kubectl --context kind-kind --namespace wallet port-forward service/grafana 3000:3000

Sign in at http://localhost:3000 as admin.

item.title: Production-ready
item.description:
The wallet and the ledger meet each item. Check your own gRPC services against them:

Item How Where
Every setting sourced and checked; a bad one exits 78, naming its variable config.Struct and the packages’ checks, in both services The wallet’s settings, The ledger’s settings
No secret in the environment, the logs or the spans PostgreSQL’s password and the private keys are files, read through s.Host.FS. The token is metadata, which otelgrpc doesn’t record, and no handler logs it, which a test of the Apps checks The secrets, as files, Their log records
Certificates and signing keys renewed without a restart internal/certfile, for both servers’ certificates and the wallet’s client certificate. The key set is fetched again for a kid the wallet lacks The certificates, read again when renewed, The fetched key set
Two replicas of each service a PodDisruptionBudget of minAvailable: 1, and a rolling update of maxUnavailable: 0 The Deployments, The disruption budgets
Ready once it has reached its dependency, and still ready through its outages Connected, and the ledger’s latch on PostgreSQL Readiness: Connected, The ledger’s probes, Readiness
A rollout loses no call grpcserver.Main’s 5s drain. A unary call is bounded by LEDGER_TIMEOUT, 10s, inside the 15s grace period. Watches end with Unavailable and are opened again. terminationGracePeriodSeconds is 30, above the drain, the grace period and the telemetry’s shutdown The drain, Relaying the watch
Calls spread across pods MaxConnectionAge on both servers MaxConnectionAge
Money is never made or lost one transaction per transfer, locks in the order of the IDs, and a CHECK that no account but external goes below zero schema.sql, A transfer’s transaction
A retry never moves money twice every transfer’s ID: the subject and the request’s ID Why every transfer is safe to retry
The contract never breaks a caller buf breaking against main, in CI buf’s rules, buf generate
Least privilege the ledger’s role has SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE on its two tables. Only the internal CA’s certificates call the ledger. A token can use only its subject’s account. A non-root, read-only container, with no service account token Running it on kind, mTLS, grpcauth, The subject’s account, The Deployments
Observable traces across both services, logs and metrics over OTLP, deploy/alerts.yaml, deploy/dashboard.json, and alerts on each Deployment from the Collector’s Kubernetes cluster receiver Observing
Failures say why statuses with PreconditionFailure, BadRequest, ErrorInfo and RetryInfo details The statuses, with details, The ledger’s answers, as the wallet’s, A key set that can’t be fetched
Failures are rehearsed the failure injection cases, in CI and against staging through its own Target The shared cases, The failure injection cases
Safe by default FAULT_TRUST_SCOPE empty, so no scenario is trusted. Server reflection off. The probes ports serve gRPC health and nothing else TrustScenario, The gRPC probes
